title: Transcendental Magic: Its Doctrine and Ritual
author: Éliphas Lévi, trans. A. E. Waite
query: Transcendental Magic Doctrine and Ritual Levi Waite
epithet: The founding book of the occult revival, in English
summary: Waite's translation of Lévi's Dogme et rituel de la haute magie — the two-part treatise, doctrine and ritual, that reinvented magic for the modern age and set the whole nineteenth-century revival in motion.

title: The Mysteries of Magic: A Digest of the Writings of Éliphas Lévi
author: A. E. Waite
query: Mysteries of Magic Digest Eliphas Levi Waite
epithet: Waite's first anthology of the great magus
summary: Waite's selection and digest of Lévi's writings, the book through which many English readers first met him — the seed of Waite's lifelong labour of translating and taming the French occultist.

title: La Science des esprits
author: Éliphas Lévi
epithet: Lévi on spirits, the Bible and the Kabbalah
summary: Lévi's late treatise reconciling his magical doctrine with the Bible and the Kabbalah, and turning a sceptical eye on the spiritism then sweeping France — a mature statement of his esoteric Catholicism.

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
epithet: Theosophy's teaching set out in order
summary: Besant's orderly exposition of the Theosophical doctrine — the planes, the bodies, karma and reincarnation — the clear textbook that carried Blavatsky's system to a mass readership.

title: Esoteric Christianity
author: Annie Besant
epithet: The lesser and greater mysteries of the Church
summary: Besant's reading of Christianity as an initiatory mystery-religion with an inner, esoteric teaching behind the exoteric creed — the Theosophical claim on the Western tradition.

title: The Astral Plane
author: C. W. Leadbeater
epithet: A clairvoyant's guide to the next world
summary: Leadbeater's description of the astral plane, its scenery and inhabitants — the founding text of Theosophical clairvoyant reportage, and a source of the modern esoteric idea of the astral.

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
epithet: The coloured plates of the human aura
summary: Leadbeater's illustrated account of the aura and subtle bodies, with its famous colour plates of thought and emotion made visible — the picture-book of Theosophical clairvoyance.

title: Knowledge of the Higher Worlds and Its Attainment
author: Rudolf Steiner
query: Knowledge of the Higher Worlds and Its Attainment Steiner
epithet: A path of training toward spiritual sight
summary: Steiner's practical course of meditative training toward higher perception — the disciplinary heart of Anthroposophy, and his most widely read book of instruction.

title: Theosophy: An Introduction
author: Rudolf Steiner
epithet: Steiner's map of the human being and destiny
summary: Steiner's introduction to the constitution of the human being, reincarnation and the path of knowledge — the doctrinal companion to his manual of training, written before his break with the Theosophists.

title: The Book of Ceremonial Magic
author: A. E. Waite
epithet: A critical survey of the grimoires
summary: Waite's examination of the grimoire tradition — the Keys of Solomon, the Grimoire of Honorius, the Grand Grimoire — reprinting their rites while insisting the true magic is within.

title: In the Pronaos of the Temple of Wisdom
author: Franz Hartmann
query: In the Pronaos of the Temple of Wisdom Hartmann
epithet: The Rosicrucian tradition, told by a theosophist
summary: Hartmann's account of the history and inner meaning of the Rosicrucian and Hermetic tradition — a bridge between the Theosophical movement and the older Western esotericism.

title: Numbers: Their Occult Power and Mystic Virtues
author: W. Wynn Westcott
query: Numbers Their Occult Power and Mystic Virtues Westcott
epithet: The Golden Dawn founder on sacred number
summary: Westcott's compendium of the mystical meanings of the numbers from Pythagoras through the Kabbalah — a small classic of number-symbolism by one of the founders of the Golden Dawn.

title: The Tarot: Its Occult Signification and Methods of Play
author: S. L. MacGregor Mathers
epithet: Mathers's little handbook of the cards
summary: Mathers's short guide to the symbolism and divinatory use of the Tarot — the compact statement of the card-lore he would build into the Golden Dawn's elaborate system.

title: The Rosicrucians: Their Rites and Mysteries
author: Hargrave Jennings
query: The Rosicrucians Their Rites and Mysteries Jennings
epithet: The book that revived the Rose Cross in England
summary: Jennings's rambling, phallic-symbolist account of the Rosicrucians and fire-worship — unreliable as history, hugely influential as the book that put the Rose Cross back into Victorian occultism.

title: Modern American Spiritualism
author: Emma Hardinge Britten
query: Modern American Spiritualism Emma Hardinge Britten
epithet: The movement's own twenty-year chronicle
summary: Britten's insider history of the first two decades of American Spiritualism, from the Fox sisters onward — the fullest contemporary record of the movement by one of its leading mediums and advocates.

title: The Principles of Nature, Her Divine Revelations
author: Andrew Jackson Davis
query: Principles of Nature Divine Revelations Andrew Jackson Davis
epithet: The Poughkeepsie Seer's dictated cosmology
summary: The vast cosmology dictated by Davis in trance — the 'Poughkeepsie Seer' whose harmonial philosophy prefigured and shaped American Spiritualism months before the Rochester rappings.
imprint: New York: S. S. Lyon and Wm. Fishbough, 1847

title: Incidents in My Life
author: Daniel Dunglas Home
query: Incidents in My Life Daniel Dunglas Home
epithet: The memoirs of the age's greatest medium
summary: The autobiography of D. D. Home, the physical medium never caught in fraud, whose levitations and séances astonished the courts of Europe — the central figure of Victorian Spiritualism in his own words.

title: Researches in the Phenomena of Spiritualism
author: William Crookes
query: Researches in the Phenomena of Spiritualism Crookes
epithet: A great chemist puts the séance to the test
summary: Crookes's report of his laboratory investigations of Home and Florence Cook — the attempt by a Fellow of the Royal Society to bring physical mediumship under experimental control, and the scandal it caused.

title: Human Personality and Its Survival of Bodily Death
author: Frederic W. H. Myers
query: Human Personality and Its Survival of Bodily Death Myers
epithet: The subliminal self and the case for survival
summary: Myers's two-volume synthesis of psychical research, proposing the 'subliminal self' and marshalling the evidence for the mind's survival of death — the founding monument of the discipline.

title: Phantasms of the Living
author: Edmund Gurney, F. W. H. Myers and Frank Podmore
query: Phantasms of the Living Gurney Myers Podmore
epithet: The great census of crisis-apparitions
summary: The Society for Psychical Research's massive two-volume study of telepathy and apparitions of the dying — hundreds of cases collected and sifted, the first attempt to make the ghost a subject of statistics.

title: Modern Spiritualism: A History and a Criticism
author: Frank Podmore
query: Modern Spiritualism History and Criticism Podmore
epithet: The sceptic's history of the movement
summary: Podmore's two-volume critical history of Spiritualism — sympathetic to the honest phenomena, merciless with the frauds — the standard scholarly account by the movement's most careful investigator.

title: The Night-Side of Nature
author: Catherine Crowe
query: The Night-Side of Nature Catherine Crowe
epithet: The book that made ghosts respectable
summary: Crowe's popular collection of hauntings, wraiths and premonitions, framed as a serious inquiry into the 'night-side' of the mind — the bestseller that prepared the English public for Spiritualism.

title: Mysterious Psychic Forces
author: Camille Flammarion
epithet: The astronomer among the mediums
summary: Flammarion's account of his decades of séance investigation, including the sittings with Eusapia Palladino — the famous astronomer lending his name to the case for unknown psychic forces.

title: The Mediums' Book
author: Allan Kardec
query: The Mediums Book Kardec Experimental Spiritism
epithet: The practical manual of Spiritism
summary: Kardec's practical sequel to The Spirits' Book — the theory and discipline of mediumship, evocation and communication that codified Spiritism into a doctrine, especially in the Latin world.

title: Esoteric Buddhism
author: A. P. Sinnett
epithet: The Mahatmas' teaching, first systematised
summary: Sinnett's systematic account of the doctrine he received in the 'Mahatma Letters' — the book that first laid out Theosophy's cosmology of rounds, races and after-death states for the public.

title: The Occult World
author: A. P. Sinnett
epithet: The book that announced the Mahatmas
summary: Sinnett's first book, publicising Blavatsky's powers and the existence of the Himalayan Masters — the work that drew a generation of the Anglo-Indian and English public toward Theosophy.

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
epithet: Theosophy in a single clear current
summary: Judge's compact, lucid exposition of the whole Theosophical teaching — long the favourite short introduction, by the American co-founder who led the movement's western wing.

title: Light on the Path
author: Mabel Collins
query: Light on the Path Mabel Collins
epithet: The small book of the rules of the Way
summary: The slender manual of aphoristic 'rules' for the aspirant on the occult path, received by Mabel Collins — a devotional classic of the Theosophical movement, memorised by generations of students.

title: Clothed with the Sun
author: Anna Kingsford
query: Clothed with the Sun Anna Kingsford
epithet: The illuminations of a Hermetic seeress
summary: The collected 'illuminations' Anna Kingsford received in vision — the esoteric Christian and Hermetic revelations that guided the Hermetic Society she and Edward Maitland founded.

title: Egyptian Magic
author: E. A. Wallis Budge
epithet: The amulets and words of power of the Nile
summary: Budge's account of Egyptian amulets, names of power, magical figures and rites — the British Museum keeper's survey that fed the Egyptian imagination of the Golden Dawn and its heirs.

title: Aradia, or the Gospel of the Witches
author: Charles Godfrey Leland
query: Aradia Gospel of the Witches Leland
epithet: The witch-gospel that seeded modern witchcraft
summary: Leland's claimed record of a surviving Tuscan witch-religion of the goddess Diana and her daughter Aradia — a slender, disputed book that became a foundation stone of twentieth-century Wicca.

title: Comment on devient mage
author: Joséphin Péladan
epithet: The aesthete-magus on becoming an adept
summary: Péladan's ethical-aesthetic manual on 'how one becomes a mage' — the manifesto of the flamboyant founder of the Salon de la Rose+Croix and the Catholic-occult decadence of 1890s Paris.

title: Au seuil du mystère
author: Stanislas de Guaita
epithet: On the threshold of the occult sciences
summary: De Guaita's introduction to the occult sciences and their literature — the opening volume of the Cabalistic Order of the Rose-Cross he founded, and the doorway to his Serpent of Genesis.

title: The Life of Paracelsus
author: Franz Hartmann
epithet: The Paracelsian revival, theosophically read
summary: Hartmann's life of Paracelsus and digest of his doctrines, presenting the Swiss physician as an adept of the occult wisdom — the book that carried Paracelsus into the Theosophical revival.

title: The Theosophical Glossary
author: H. P. Blavatsky
epithet: The lexicon of the whole secret doctrine
summary: Blavatsky's posthumous dictionary of the Sanskrit, Hebrew, Kabbalistic and occult terms strewn through her work — the key readers needed to follow the Secret Doctrine, and a map of her sources.

title: Konx Om Pax
author: Aleister Crowley
epithet: Essays in the light, from the young magus
summary: Crowley's playful, elaborately produced volume of mystical essays and verse — 'essays in light' from the period just before he proclaimed the Law of Thelema, and a specimen of his early adepthood.

title: Fortune-Telling Cards: The Tarot
author: S. L. MacGregor Mathers
epithet: The card-lore of the Golden Dawn's chief
summary: Mathers's illustrated treatment of the Tarot for divination — the popular face of the elaborate esoteric card-system he devised for the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn.

title: Art Magic
author: Emma Hardinge Britten
epithet: Mundane, submundane and supermundane spiritism
summary: The anonymous treatise Britten edited and published on the whole range of magic and spirit-intercourse across history — an ambitious esoteric synthesis that predated and rivalled Blavatsky's Isis.

title: After Death — What?
author: Cesare Lombroso
epithet: The criminologist converted by the séance
summary: Lombroso's account of the spiritistic phenomena — above all the mediumship of Eusapia Palladino — that turned the famous positivist criminologist into a reluctant believer late in life.

title: Histoire et doctrine des Rose-Croix
author: Paul Sédir
epithet: The French revival's history of the Rose Cross
summary: Sédir's history and doctrine of the Rosicrucians — a product of the Papus circle that shaped how the French occult revival understood its own Rosicrucian ancestry.

title: First Principles of Theosophy
author: C. Jinarajadasa
epithet: The teaching drawn together for the student
summary: Jinarajadasa's ordered survey of the Theosophical doctrine, richly diagrammed — the standard study-course of the Adyar society in the years of its greatest reach.

title: ABC illustré d'occultisme
author: Papus
epithet: A first primer of the occult sciences
summary: Papus's illustrated beginner's primer of occultism — Kabbalah, astrology, Tarot and magic in outline — the entry-level companion to his great methodical treatise.

title: People from the Other World
author: Henry Steel Olcott
query: People from the Other World Olcott
epithet: The investigations that led to the Theosophical Society
summary: Olcott's reports of the Eddy-farm materialisations, where he met Blavatsky — the séance investigations that led directly to the founding of the Theosophical Society the following year.

title: Mysticism
author: Evelyn Underhill
epithet: The classic modern study of the mystic way
summary: Underhill's great study of the nature and stages of the mystical life — awakening, purgation, illumination, the dark night and union — the standard English account for a century.

title: Footfalls on the Boundary of Another World
author: Robert Dale Owen
query: Footfalls on the Boundary of Another World Owen
epithet: A statesman's dossier of the spirit-world
summary: Owen's carefully documented collection of apparitions, hauntings and spirit-manifestations — the book by a former US congressman that gave American Spiritualism an air of respectability.

title: The History of Spiritualism
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
query: The History of Spiritualism Conan Doyle
epithet: Sherlock Holmes's creator as the movement's evangelist
summary: Doyle's two-volume history and defence of Spiritualism, from the Fox sisters to his own day — the great convert's committed account of the movement he spent his last years championing.

title: Raymond, or Life and Death
author: Oliver Lodge
query: Raymond or Life and Death Oliver Lodge
epithet: A physicist's contact with his son beyond death
summary: The physicist Oliver Lodge's account of the séance messages he believed came from his son Raymond, killed in the war — the book that made survival after death a national conversation in wartime Britain.

title: On the Threshold of the Unseen
author: William F. Barrett
query: On the Threshold of the Unseen Barrett
epithet: A founder of the SPR weighs the evidence
summary: Barrett's summing-up of the evidence for survival and psychical phenomena — by the physicist whose 1876 paper led to the founding of the Society for Psychical Research.

title: Death — and After?
author: Annie Besant
epithet: The Theosophical map of the after-death states
summary: Besant's little manual of the Theosophical teaching on death and the states beyond it — kamaloka, devachan and the soul's journey — one of the movement's most reprinted primers.

title: The Growth of the Soul
author: A. P. Sinnett
query: The Growth of the Soul Sinnett
epithet: The sequel to Esoteric Buddhism
summary: Sinnett's continuation of his Theosophical exposition, developing the doctrine of the soul's evolution through many lives and planes — a fuller statement of the teaching of the Mahatma letters.
